name: gzip
purpose: GNU Zip — compress files to reduce their size (creating .gz files) or decompress them.
explanation: Compresses a file using the DEFLATE algorithm and replaces the original file with a smaller compressed version ending in '.gz'. To restore the original file, use 'gzip -d' (or 'gunzip'). Note that gzip compresses individual files rather than bundling folders together (for folders, combine with 'tar' first).

parameters.description: Decompresses a .gz file back to its original uncompressed form.
Keep — retains the original file instead of deleting it after compression or decompression.
Verbose — prints the filename and percentage size reduction.
Recursive — compresses every file inside a directory individually.

expectedOutput: (Creates notes.txt.gz while keeping notes.txt, then decompresses it back)
whenToUse: When you want to shrink large text files, logs, or backups to save disk space or speed up transfers.
commonMistakes: Running 'gzip file.txt' without -k and being surprised that the original file.txt was replaced by file.txt.gz.
Trying to compress an entire folder into a single archive with plain gzip (use tar -czf archive.tar.gz folder/ for multi-file archives).
